administrators.name: Robert Clive
administrators.note: Company administration in Bengal expanded after Plassey.

administrators.name: Henry Vansittart
administrators.note: Served during the period leading to Buxar and the Diwani settlement.

administrators.name: Robert Clive
administrators.note: Returned to Bengal and implemented the dual system.

administrators.name: Harry Verelst
administrators.note: Company governor during a period of major revenue and administrative strain.

administrators.name: John Cartier
administrators.note: In office during the Bengal famine and the lead-up to parliamentary intervention.

administrators.name: Warren Hastings
administrators.note: First Governor-General under the Regulating Act of 1773.

administrators.name: John Macpherson (acting)
administrators.note: Acted after Hastings and before Cornwallis.

administrators.name: Charles Cornwallis
administrators.note: Associated with the Permanent Settlement of 1793.

administrators.name: John Shore
administrators.note: Later created Baron Teignmouth.

administrators.name: Richard Wellesley
administrators.note: Expanded Company influence through subsidiary alliances.

administrators.name: Charles Cornwallis (second term)
administrators.note: Briefly returned to office in 1805 and died in India.

administrators.name: George Barlow (acting)
administrators.note: Acted between Cornwallis and Minto.

administrators.name: Gilbert Elliot-Murray-Kynynmound (Minto I)
administrators.note: Oversaw the Company during the Napoleonic era.

administrators.name: Francis Rawdon-Hastings (Lord Hastings)
administrators.note: Served during the Third Anglo-Maratha War.

administrators.name: William Amherst
administrators.note: In office during the First Anglo-Burmese War.

administrators.name: William Bentinck
administrators.note: Associated with administrative and social reforms; the office title changed in the 1830s.

administrators.name: Charles Metcalfe (acting)
administrators.note: Acting office-holder after Bentinck.

administrators.name: George Eden (Lord Auckland)
administrators.note: In office during the First Anglo-Afghan War.

administrators.name: Edward Law (Lord Ellenborough)
administrators.note: Oversaw the withdrawal from Afghanistan and the conquest of Sindh period.

administrators.name: Henry Hardinge
administrators.note: In office during the First Anglo-Sikh War.

administrators.name: James Andrew Broun-Ramsay (Lord Dalhousie)
administrators.note: Associated with annexation policies and major infrastructural expansion.

administrators.name: Charles Canning
administrators.office: Governor-General of India; first Viceroy from 1858
administrators.note: Served through the 1857 uprising and the transfer from Company to Crown rule.

administrators.name: James Bruce (Lord Elgin I)
administrators.note: Died while in office.

administrators.name: Robert Napier (acting)
administrators.note: Brief acting term.

administrators.name: William Denison (acting)
administrators.note: Acted until John Lawrence took office.

administrators.name: John Lawrence
administrators.note: Formerly Chief Commissioner of Punjab.

administrators.name: Richard Bourke (Lord Mayo)
administrators.note: Assassinated at Port Blair in 1872.

administrators.name: John Strachey (acting)
administrators.note: Brief acting term following Mayo's death.

administrators.name: Thomas Baring (Lord Northbrook)
administrators.note: Resigned in 1876.

administrators.name: Edward Robert Lytton (Lord Lytton)
administrators.note: In office during the Second Anglo-Afghan War and the 1876 Delhi Durbar.

administrators.name: George Robinson (Lord Ripon)
administrators.note: Introduced local-self-government reforms and repealed the Vernacular Press Act.

administrators.name: Frederick Hamilton-Temple-Blackwood (Lord Dufferin)
administrators.note: In office when the Indian National Congress was founded.

administrators.name: Henry Petty-Fitzmaurice (Lord Lansdowne)
administrators.note: Oversaw the Indian Councils Act 1892 period.

administrators.name: Victor Bruce (Lord Elgin II)
administrators.note: Served during famine and plague crises.

administrators.name: George Nathaniel Curzon
administrators.note: Partitioned Bengal in 1905.

administrators.name: Gilbert Elliot-Murray-Kynynmound (Minto II)
administrators.note: In office during the Morley–Minto reforms.

administrators.name: Charles Hardinge (Hardinge II)
administrators.note: Announced the capital shift to Delhi in 1911.

administrators.name: Frederic Thesiger (Lord Chelmsford)
administrators.note: In office during the Rowlatt Act and Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

administrators.name: Rufus Isaacs (Lord Reading)
administrators.note: Served during the Non-Cooperation era.

administrators.name: Edward Wood (Lord Irwin; later Lord Halifax)
administrators.note: In office during the Salt March and Gandhi–Irwin Pact.

administrators.name: Freeman-Thomas (Lord Willingdon)
administrators.note: Served during the Civil Disobedience movement and Poona Pact.

administrators.name: Victor Hope (Lord Linlithgow)
administrators.note: Longest-serving viceroy; in office during World War II and Quit India.

administrators.name: Archibald Wavell
administrators.note: Oversaw the Simla Conference and early transfer negotiations.

administrators.name: Louis Mountbatten
administrators.office: Last Viceroy and Governor-General of British India
administrators.note: Oversaw the 3 June Plan and the transfer of power.

administrators.name: Louis Mountbatten
administrators.office: Governor-General of the Dominion of India
administrators.note: Continued as Governor-General after independence.

administrators.name: C. Rajagopalachari
administrators.office: Governor-General of the Dominion of India
administrators.note: The only Indian to hold the office and the last Governor-General of India.

administrators.name: Rajendra Prasad
administrators.office: President of the Republic of India
administrators.note: India became a republic; the Governor-General's office ended.
